I understand how strong the stigma against male victims must feel to you right now, but what others have said on here is right on. \*You\* have nothing to be ashamed of, \*you\* did nothing wrong, and you deserve to be believed. Anyone who mocks or makes light of you are not friends worth having.

Licensing is different across all provinces. Since 2009, in Quebec, social workers need a psychotherapy permit to practice certain reserved therapeutic acts (thanks to a lot of lobbying by a predominantly male order of psychologists). You need to complete additional supervisional hours for that. However, social workers have protected titles themselves, and that comes with its own union benefits. Plus, most social workers do a lot of "supportive counselling" without calling themselves psychotherapists.

Canadian degrees are I think more transferable across provinces. Some boards will license you on the basis of documented experience even if your diploma doesn't match their educational requirements. But if you have a university degree, you are pretty much a candidate for licensure anywhere.
